question.prompt: The weight of \(\tfrac13\) of a large pizza together with \(3\tfrac12\) cups of orange slices is the same as the weight of \(\tfrac34\) of a large pizza together with \(\tfrac12\) cup of orange slices. A cup of orange slices weighs \(\tfrac14\) of a pound. What is the weight, in pounds, of a large pizza?

solutions.title: Compare the extra amounts
solutions.explanation:
Removing the same food amounts from two equal-weight combinations preserves their equality. Remove \(\tfrac13\) of a pizza and \(\tfrac12\) cup of orange slices from each combination.

The first combination now contains \(3\) cups of orange slices. The second contains
\[
\frac34-\frac13=\frac9{12}-\frac4{12}=\frac5{12}
\]
of a pizza. Therefore \(\tfrac5{12}\) of the pizza weighs as much as \(3\) cups of orange slices, namely
\[
3\cdot\frac14=\frac34\text{ pound}.
\]
Dividing by the fraction of the pizza gives the whole pizza's weight:
\[
\frac34\div\frac5{12}
=\frac34\cdot\frac{12}{5}
=\frac95
=\boxed{1\frac45}\text{ pounds}.
\]
The answer is choice A.
